label: History
value: The Lion bounded onto the road of yellow brick.
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, the Lion bounded onto the road of yellow brick, knocking over the Scarecrow and striking the Tin Woodman. When he attempted to bite Toto, Dorothy slapped his nose and called him a coward, which he shamefully acknowledged. Learning that Dorothy and her companions were traveling to see the Great Oz to ask for their desires, the Lion decided to join them to ask Oz for courage. During their journey, he grew close to Dorothy and became good friends with Toto. While passing through a poppy field, he succumbed to the powerful scent of the flowers and fell asleep, but he was saved from death by an army of field mice. Upon reaching the Emerald City and eventually obtaining an audience with Oz, he was given a liquid in a dish to drink, which Oz claimed was courage; drinking it left him feeling full of courage and happy.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived in Kansas with her Aunt Em and Uncle Henry
unit: Dorothy lived in Kansas with her Aunt Em and Uncle Henry until a cyclone swept her house into the air with her and her dog Toto inside. Upon her arrival in the Land of Oz, she obtained the Silver Shoes and set out to find the Great Wizard Oz in the Emerald City to seek a way home. Accompanied by her dog and companions she met along the way, she was granted an audience with Oz, who appeared to her as a giant Head. Oz promised to return her to Kansas on the condition that she kill the Wicked Witch of the West. Saddened by the task, she was captured by the Wicked Witch and forced to do heavy kitchen work while secretly feeding her imprisoned friend, the Cowardly Lion, each night. When the Witch used a trick to steal one of her Silver Shoes, Dorothy confronted her in anger.

label: History
value: Glinda is the Witch of the South
unit: Glinda, the Witch of the South and the most powerful of all witches, established her rule over the Quadlings from her beautiful castle located on the edge of the desert. When Dorothy and her companions traveled to the South Country seeking a way for Dorothy to return to Kansas, Glinda granted them an immediate audience in her throne room. After hearing Dorothy's tale, Glinda offered to reveal how Dorothy could return home in exchange for the Golden Cap. Upon receiving the Cap, Glinda promised to use its three commands to carry the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the land of the Winkies, and the Cowardly Lion to his forest, before giving the Cap to the King of the Monkeys to free them forever. She then informed Dorothy that her Silver Shoes possessed the power to carry her anywhere in three steps. After bidding a affectionate good-bye to Dorothy with a kiss, Glinda watched as the girl used the shoes to return to Kansas.

She then informed Dorothy that her Silver Shoes possessed the power to carry her anywhere in three steps. After bidding a affectionate good-bye to Dorothy with a kiss, Glinda watched as the girl used the shoes to return to Kansas.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow was originally placed on a pole in a cornfield.
unit: The Scarecrow was originally placed on a pole in a cornfield until Dorothy rescued him and lifted him down. Eager to obtain brains, he agreed to join Dorothy on her journey along the yellow brick road to see the Great Oz in the Emerald City. Along the way, he met the Tin Woodman and supported his addition to their party. When the group encountered a densely overgrown path, he watched as the Tin Woodman cleared the way, and later stumbled into a hole because he lacked the knowledge to walk around it. Upon reaching a farmhouse near the Emerald City, he requested brains from the Wizard during their discussions, though he did not need to eat or sleep during their overnight stay. After arriving at the Emerald City and later assuming leadership, he continued to seek ways to assist Dorothy. When Oz could not send Dorothy home, the Scarecrow reasoned that traveling south to seek Glinda's help was her best option and pledged to accompany her until she safely reached Kansas. During their journey to the South, he led the travelers up a steep, rocky hill inhabited by the Hammer-Heads. Unaware of their abilities, he walked forward to pass them, only to be struck by a Hammer-Head's shooting head and sent tumbling down the hill. After Dorothy helped him up, the party used the Winged Monkeys to fly over the hill into Quadling Country, where they stopped at a farmhouse for food and directions.

value: The Tin Woodman originally worked as a human wood-chopper.
unit: The Tin Woodman originally worked as a human wood-chopper who fell in love with a beautiful Munchkin maiden. To stop their marriage, an old woman conspired with the Wicked Witch of the East, who enchanted his axe to sever his limbs and body. A tinsmith replaced each lost part with tin until he was made entirely of metal, but without a heart, he lost his love for the maiden. After rusting motionless in the woods for a year during a rainstorm, he was rescued by Dorothy and the Scarecrow. He joined their party on the yellow brick road to seek a heart from Oz in the Emerald City. Along the way, he used his axe to clear paths, chopped off the head of a Wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, and built a ladder to help the group scale a high white china wall.

label: History
value: Oz is originally from Omaha.
unit: Originally a ventriloquist and balloonist from Omaha, Oz accidentally drifted into the Land of Oz when his hot-air balloon's ropes became twisted. The local inhabitants believed he was a great wizard descended from the clouds, so he took on the role of their ruler and ordered the construction of the Emerald City. To preserve his secret as a humbug without actual magical powers, he hid in his Throne Room and used clever mechanical devices and ventriloquism to appear to visitors as a giant Head, a lovely Lady, a terrible Beast, or a Ball of Fire. When Dorothy and her companions arrived seeking favors, he demanded they first kill the Wicked Witch of the West. After Dorothy melted the Witch and exposed his true identity, Oz fulfilled his companions' wishes through clever improvisations: giving the Scarecrow a brain of bran and pins, the Tin Woodman a silk-and-sawdust heart, and the Lion a potion of courage. He then constructed a new hot-air balloon to escape back to Omaha with Dorothy. However, when Dorothy delayed to find Toto, the ropes snapped, and Oz floated away alone, leaving the Scarecrow appointed as the new ruler of the Emerald City.

To preserve his secret as a humbug without actual magical powers, he hid in his Throne Room and used clever mechanical devices and ventriloquism to appear to visitors as a giant Head, a lovely Lady, a terrible Beast, or a Ball of Fire. When Dorothy and her companions arrived seeking favors, he demanded they first kill the Wicked Witch of the West. After Dorothy melted the Witch and exposed his true identity, Oz fulfilled his companions' wishes through clever improvisations: giving the Scarecrow a brain of bran and pins, the Tin Woodman a silk-and-sawdust heart, and the Lion a potion of courage. He then constructed a new hot-air balloon to escape back to Omaha with Dorothy. However, when Dorothy delayed to find Toto, the ropes snapped, and Oz floated away alone, leaving the Scarecrow appointed as the new ruler of the Emerald City.
